reason: The authors train classification baselines including EfficientNet, Inception and MobileViT, and prompt the Molmo-7B VLM with SAM for zero-shot segmentation.
Brain-TIM uses modality-specific embedding layers and a Time Interval MLP module, and the text names no transformer or other named family.
The proposed decision-aware training is applied to a negative binomial mixed effects regression model, and EpiGNN appears only as a compared baseline.
IDEAS uses an explainable model to guide mutations but the excerpt never names its architecture; ESM-2 with a linear layer serves only as the evaluation oracle.
NCfold is a transformer with REF-weighted self-attention over frozen RNA foundation model embeddings, and these are not natural-language LLMs.
EEG is encoded with a CNN-Transformer (EEG-Conformer) encoder and decoded by a convolutional VAE decoder with transposed convolutions.
SASHA uses a pre-trained ViT feature extractor with a multi-head attention feature distiller, and the RL policy network family is not named.
A CNN core-readout predictive model is trained jointly with a multivariate Student t mixture clustering model fitted by EM.
The source model is a DeiT-base network and the GUES generator is an eight-layer convolutional VAE.
The GFlowNet policy is a two-layer LSTM and the proxy models are parameterized as CNN ensembles.
AtlasSegFM adapts frozen segmentation foundation models with a registration network and a lightweight 3D encoder, but none of their families are named.
Forecastability fine-tuning is applied with LoRA to the Qwen3-0.6B language model and to a small task-conditioned U-Net RL policy.
NEvo fits voxel-wise ridge regressions on V-JEPA 2 features and generates videos with the LTX-Video diffusion transformer.
The authors train a GNN, a 3D-CNN, and MLP heads on pretrained Uni-Mol and ProFSA encoders whose families are not named.
Var-JEPA uses MLP-based variational encoders, Var-T-JEPA uses attention-based token pooling and mask tokens, and XGBoost is among the downstream predictors on the embeddings.
Aegis generates defense data with a pretrained latent diffusion model, and the federated model architecture is not named in the text.
The authors train a ResNet18 image encoder, a CNN text encoder and MLP encoders and regressors; CLIP appears only in a case study.
MethylProphet is a transformer encoder, and its bottleneck MLP is a sub-module of that same model.
Pancakes uses a UNet-like convolutional architecture with convolutional layers and skip connections.
DSRF is built from custom gated attention reasoning blocks and Gram matrices, with CNNs and MLPs mentioned only as prior work and ablation alternatives.
